# Background

This follows the [RPub](https://rpubs.com/andresmtnezglez/1040031) tutorial.

In this example we will generate random variables following $Y \sim N(4,5)$. Then, we will pretend we don't know the true values and aim to find the distribution parameters for $Y \sim N(\mu, \sigma)$.

```{r generating_obs}
set.seed(78)

n_obs <- 1000
true_mu <- 3
true_sig <- 2

obs <- rnorm(n_obs, mean=true_mu, sd=true_sig)
mean_obs <- mean(obs) 

hist(obs, main="Histogram of Observed Data", ylab="Frequency", xlab="Value",col = "#BBD7EA", border = "white", "FD")
```
# Finding Conditionals

We need to actually set up functions for our gibbs sampler to use, so it can properly traveerse the parameter space.

## Priors (conjugate)

For our mean, we choose a normal distribution.

$$ 
\mu \sim N(\mu_{\mu}, \sigma_{\mu})
$$

```{r plot_mean_prior}
mean_data <- rnorm(1000, mean=1, sd=3)

hist(mean_data, main = "N(1,3) Distribution", xlab = "Value", ylab="Frequency")
abline(v = 3, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```
For our standard deviation, we choose the Gamma distribution, which makes sense since the value cannot be negative.

$$ 
\sigma \sim \text{Gamma}(a, b)
$$

```{r plot_mean_prior}
gamma_data <- rgamma(1000, 1, 1)

hist(gamma_data, main = "Gamma(1,1) Distribution", xlab = "Value", ylab="Frequency")
abline(v = (1/4)**2, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```
```{r}
library(latex2exp)
old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(8, 4, 3, 1), bg = "white")

hist(gamma_data, "FD",
     main = TeX(r"($\tau \sim$Gamma(1, 1))"),
     xlab = "Value", ylab = "Frequency",
     col = "#BBD7EA", border = "white")
abline(v = (1/2)**2, col = "#C43C39", lwd = 3)

hist(mean_data, "FD",
     main = TeX(r"($\mu \sim$Normal(1, 3))"),
     xlab = "Value",
     col = "#BBD7EA", border = "white")
abline(v = 3, col = "#C43C39", lwd = 3)

par(old_par)
```
## Conditionals

This is found by following:

$$
\begin{align*}
\underbrace{P(\vec{\theta}| \vec{Y})}_{\text{Posterior}} &\propto \underbrace{P(\vec{Y}|\vec{\theta})}_{Likelihood} \underbrace{P(\vec{\theta})}_{Priors}\\
\Rightarrow P(\vec{\theta}|\vec{Y}) &\propto \underbrace{P(\vec{Y}, \vec{\theta})}_{Joint}
\end{align*} 
$$

Then pulling the two conditionals out of the joint! The best way to ensure this remains normalized is by shoving this into a known distribution's form.

Note: $\tau = \frac{1}{var(y)}$.

The tutorial did the heavy lifting for us and derived bot conditionals, shown below:

$$
\mu|\tau,y \sim N\left( \frac{n\bar{y}\tau+\mu_{\mu}\tau_{\mu}}{n\tau+\tau_{\mu}}, n\tau+\tau_{\mu} \right)
$$

$$
\sigma|\mu,y \sim Gamma\left(a+n/2,b+\frac{1}{2}\sum_i(y_i-\mu)^2\right)
$$
# Gibbs Sampling

Below is the code to set up the general Gibbs sampler.
```{r}
# Actual Gibb Sampling function - input is the last position in param space
gibbs_sampler <- function(last_mu, last_tau,
                          arb_constants, obs) { # will need to define how
                                           # arb constants need to be saved
  # set up for mu calculation
  mu_mean <-  ((sum(obs)*last_tau)+(arb_constants$mu_mu*arb_constants$tau_mu))/
                        ((n_obs*last_tau)+arb_constants$tau_mu)
  mu_tau <- (n_obs*last_tau) + arb_constants$tau_mu
  mu <- rnorm(1, mean=mu_mean, sd = 1/sqrt(mu_tau)) # I think
  
  # set up for sigma calculation
  shape <- arb_constants$a + (n_obs)/2
  rate <- arb_constants$b + 0.5*(sum((obs - mu)**2))
  tau <- rgamma(1, shape, rate)
  
  # returning the new sample - in an end-user friendly manner
  return(list(mu=mu, tau=tau)) 
}

```

After setting up the function we can actually run the simulation:

```{r simulation}

run_gibb <- function (inital_mu, inital_tau, arb_constants,
                      obs=NULL, runs=5000, seed=666) {
  
  set.seed(seed)
  samples <- matrix(NA, nrow=runs, ncol=2,
                    dimnames = list(NULL, c("mu", "tau"))) # user friendly?
  
  start_mu <- inital_mu
  start_tau <- inital_tau
    
  for (i in 1:runs) {
    #sampling and saving
    gibber <- gibbs_sampler(start_mu, start_tau, arb_constants, obs=obs)
    samples[i,1] <- gibber$mu
    samples[i,2] <-gibber$tau
    
    # Updating the initalization values
    start_mu <- gibber$mu
    start_tau <- gibber$tau
  }
  
  return(list(mu=samples[,1], tau=samples[,2]))
}

# Function to ensure your constants are in a function friendly format
save_constants <- function(sampler="norm_conj", #sampler
                           mu_mu=0, tau_mu=0.05, a=3, b=2, #normal conjugate
                           test=0) {
  if (sampler == "norm_conj") {
      return(list(mu_mu=mu_mu, tau_mu=tau_mu, a=a, b=b))
  } else if (sampler == "test") {
      print("bleh")
      return(list=test)
  }
}

burn_it <- function(samples, burn_len=500) {
  return(samples[burn_len:length(samples)])
}


```

## Assessing Convergence

Below is the function to actually run the trace plot:

```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
runs <- 50000
init_mu <- mean(obs)
init_tau <- 1 / var(obs)

# note: this actually didn't converge with 2 or 3 as the mean wtf
arb_constants <- save_constants("norm_conj", 1, 3, 1, 1) # the defaults are best tbh
samples <- run_gibb(init_mu, init_tau, arb_constants, obs=obs, runs=runs)

trace_conj <- func(samples) {
  trace_data <- data.frame(
    iteration = seq_along(samples$mu),
    mu = samples$mu,
    tau = samples$tau
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(iteration %% 5 == 0) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(mu, tau),
                        names_to = "parameter",
                        values_to = "draw")
  
    reference <- data.frame(
      parameter = c("mu", "tau"),
      true_value = c(true_mu, 1/(true_sig**2))
    )
  
    strip_labels <- c(
      mu = '"Sampled" ~ mu',
      tau = '"Sampled" ~ tau'
    )
  
    ggplot(trace_data, aes(x = iteration, y = draw)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_hline(
        data = reference,
        aes(yintercept = true_value),
        colour = "firebrick",
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      facet_wrap(
        ~ parameter,
        ncol = 1,
        labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels, default = label_parsed),
        scales = "free_y"
      ) +
      labs(x = "Gibbs iteration", y = "Sampled value") +
      theme_minimal()
}

```
## Putting this all together

Below is the usage of all the functions
```{r}
hist(burn_it(samples$mu, burn_len=1000), "FD",
     main = TeX(r"(Samples of $\mu$)"),
     xlab = "Value", ylab = "Frequency",
     col = "#BBD7EA", border = "white")
```
```{r}
hist(burn_it(samples$tau), "FD",
     main = TeX(r"(Samples of $\tau$)"),
     xlab = "Value", ylab = "Frequency",
     col = "#BBD7EA", border = "white")
```
